Empirical Research Plan – Long-Run Stock Performance after IPO  

=====================================================================

1. Identification Strategy  
   • Method: Event–time Difference-in-Differences (DID) / Event-study.  
   • Rationale:  
     – Each IPO gives a clean, single-day “adoption” date that is staggered across calendar time (1970-1990).  
     – We have repeated‐measure outcomes (monthly returns) for both newly public and already-public firms.  
     – By comparing the post-IPO return path of the treated firms with a matched set of established firms observed over the same calendar months we can difference out aggregate market shocks and isolate the incremental “going-public” effect.  
     – The design can be implemented either as (i) a traditional event-study of abnormal returns (BHAR) or (ii) a modern staggered-adoption DID with firm and calendar-month fixed effects (e.g., Callaway & Sant’Anna 2021, Sun & Abraham 2021). I will use the latter because it delivers unbiased ATT estimates and allows visual pre-trend checks.

2. Treatment and Control  
   • Treatment variable: IPO_it = 1 if firm i is within the 36-month window after its first IPO date, 0 otherwise.  
   • Treatment timing: Event date t = 0 is the first trading day after the IPO. “Post” is months +1 to +36; months –36 to –1 are pre.  
   • Control group (counterfactual): Public firms that did **not** issue an IPO in the sample window. For each IPO we select up to three controls matched on:  
        – Same 2-digit SIC industry  
        – Market-cap decile in the month before the IPO  
        – Pre-event beta (estimated from 36-month window ending −2)  
     Matching is done with replacement (nearest-neighbor Mahalanobis + caliper). After matching, all control firms are given the **same event-time zero** as the treated firm they are matched to, so we can run a stacked panel DID.  
   • Outcome: Monthly log return or abnormal return (actual minus predicted from Fama-French 3-factor model).  
   • No running variable/cutoff is required (not an RDD).

3. Key Identifying Assumptions  
   A1. Parallel trends in the absence of treatment. Matched established firms should follow the same return path that IPO firms would have followed had they stayed private. Plausible because we match tightly on industry, size, and beta, and we include month fixed effects to soak up market-wide shocks.  
   A2. No differential anticipation. Private information leakages would mainly influence the IPO pricing window (t = –1 to +1); our long-run window starts at +1 month, so anticipation is limited.  
   A3. Stable Unit Treatment Value (SUTVA). An IPO by firm i does not materially affect the return of its matched controls (minimal product-market spillovers at the industry/year scale).  
   A4. Composition stability. Delistings during the three-year window must be accounted for; we keep them in the panel with returns carried forward at delisting price to avoid attrition bias.  
   A5. Risk adjustment sufficiency. Using factor-model abnormal returns plus firm fixed effects removes time-varying risk differences that could masquerade as under- or out-performance.

4. Threats to Identification & Mitigation  
   1. Endogenous selection into IPO (better or worse firms self-select).  
        – Mitigation: tight ex-ante matching; include pre-event firm covariates; show balance statistics; run propensity-score-weighted DID as robustness.  
   2. Differential risk evolution post-IPO (treatment firms may systematically change leverage or R&D intensity).  
        – Mitigation: compute both raw and factor-adjusted abnormal returns; interact treatment with time-varying betas; test whether post-IPO risk premia explain results.  
   3. Attrition (delisting, mergers, bankruptcy).  
        – Mitigation: follow‐to‐delist with terminal return; use inverse-probability-of-censoring weights; show results excluding early delisters.

5. R Code Outline  

```r
# -------------- 0. Packages -----------------
library(data.table)   # fast data handling
library(fixest)       # high-dim FE regressions
library(MatchIt)      # matching
library(did)          # staggered-adoption DID
library(ggplot2)

# -------------- 1. Load data ----------------
# File contains: permno, date, return, mktcap, sic, IPO_date (NA if never IPO)
raw <- fread("ipo_panel_1970_1990.csv")

# Convert to monthly time-series
raw[, month := as.Date(format(date, "%Y-%m-01"))]

# -------------- 2. Create treatment window ---
# months relative to first IPO trading date
raw[, month_rel := as.integer(12 * (as.yearmon(month) - as.yearmon(IPO_date)))]
raw <- raw[month_rel >= -36 & month_rel <= 36]   # keep ±36 window

# Indicator variables
raw[, treat := as.integer(!is.na(IPO_date))]
raw[, post  := as.integer(month_rel >= 1 & month_rel <= 36)]
raw[, treat_post := treat * post]

# -------------- 3. Matching ------------------
# One row per firm at event time −1 for matching
pre <- unique(raw[month_rel == -1,
                  .(permno, sic2 = substr(sic,1,2), size = log(mktcap),
                    beta_pre = beta_pre, treat)])

# Estimate propensity to be treated
m.out <- matchit(treat ~ factor(sic2) + size + beta_pre,
                 data = pre, method = "nearest", ratio = 3)
matched_ids  <- data.table(permno = rownames(m.out$match.matrix))
raw <- raw[permno %in% c(pre[treat==1,permno], matched_ids$permno)]

# -------------- 4. Outcome construction ------
# Abnormal return: actual minus expected from FF3 (pre-computed FF factors)
ff <- fread("ff_monthly.csv")
raw <- merge(raw, ff, by = "month", all.x = TRUE)

# Estimate rolling betas (pre-IPO)
# ... code omitted for brevity ...
raw[, abret := return - (rf + beta_m * (rmrf) + beta_smb * smb + beta_hml * hml)]

# -------------- 5. Main FE DID ---------------
est <- feols(abret ~ treat_post | permno + month,
             data = raw, cluster = ~permno)
summary(est)

# -------------- 6. Event-study graph ---------
ev <- feols(abret ~ i(month_rel, treat, ref = -1) | permno + month,
            data = raw, cluster = ~permno)
iplot(ev, xlab="Months from IPO", ylab="Abnormal return")

# -------------- 7. Robustness: Callaway & Sant’Anna ----
cs <- att_gt(yname = "abret", gname = "IPO_date", idname = "permno",
             tname = "month", xformla = ~size + beta_pre,
             data = raw)
aggte_out <- aggte(cs, type = "dynamic")
ggdid(aggte_out)   # plot dynamic ATTs
```

6. Expected Results  
   Prior finance literature finds that IPOs tend to **under-perform** by roughly 20–30 percentage points on a buy-and-hold basis over the first three years (≈ –0.5 % abnormal return per month). I expect a cumulative ATT of about −0.20 (log-return units) by month 36.

7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (DID)  
   C1: Clear, exogenous event date (IPO)……………… 1  
   C2: Pre-treatment parallel trend evidence………… 0.8 (will test)  
   C3: No anticipation / contamination…………………… 0.8  
   C4: Stable composition & no spillovers……………… 0.7  
   C5: Correct inference (clustering, staggered)……… 1  
   Average ≈ 0.86 → design is reasonably credible, but hinges on demonstrated pre-trend balance and attrition adjustments.
